title: Antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations: pairing and evidence
summary: How repulsive interactions can favor sign-changing gaps, why magnetic signals do not prove a mechanism, and how probe limits and published corrections constrain the evidence.

claims.statement: Antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations are a candidate pairing interaction with substantial weight at a nonzero momentum transfer. A repulsive interaction can favor a gap that changes sign between the states it connects. This is a model-dependent mechanism proposal: observing magnetism, or finding superconductivity near an antiferromagnetic phase, does not establish causation.

claims.statement: A local static illustration, checked by separate matrix calculations, uses two patches with positive single-spin density-of-states weights $N_h,N_e$, a common pairing cutoff, constant gaps and real reciprocal interactions $U_h,U_e,V\ge0$. After the common energy logarithm is factored out, define $\eta\Delta_i=-\sum_jV_{ij}N_j\Delta_j$, with $V_{he}=V_{eh}=V$. The rescaling $x_i=\sqrt{N_i}\Delta_i$ gives a symmetric matrix with diagonal elements $-U_iN_i$ and off-diagonal element $-V\sqrt{N_hN_e}$. This is a separate static model, not a reduction validated against the review's dynamical calculation.

claims.statement: For nonnegative intrapatch repulsions it is positive precisely when $V^2>U_hU_e$. The trace is nonpositive and the determinant is $(U_hU_e-V^2)N_hN_e$, establishing this threshold within the two-dimensional model. If both $U_i$ vanish and $V>0$, $\eta_+=V\sqrt{N_hN_e}$ and $\Delta_h/\Delta_e=-\sqrt{N_e/N_h}$. If all interactions vanish, the kernel is zero and no preferred gap ratio is selected. A 432-case check compares direct and symmetrized eigensolvers, exact rational determinants and threshold cases. These are illustrative pairing strengths, not the phonon spectral coupling $\lambda$, a calculated transition temperature, or a fit to any material.

claims.statement: A second independent check shows why a wavevector alone cannot select the gap symmetry. With lattice spacing one, both $\cos k_x-\cos k_y$ and $\cos k_x+\cos k_y$ reverse sign under $\mathbf Q=(\pi,\pi)$. Under a ninety-degree rotation the former changes sign while the latter does not. Their values on the actual Fermi surface and their interaction-weighted eigenvalues still differ. A sign-reversal condition is therefore insufficient to select a unique representation.

claims.statement: Neutron, RIXS and NMR measurements have different response functions, selection rules and energy windows. In the magnetic low-frequency limit, NMR relaxation has the schematic dependence $1/(T_1T)\propto\sum_{\mathbf q,\alpha\perp H}|A_\alpha(\mathbf q)|^2\lim_{\omega\to0}\chi''_\alpha(\mathbf q,\omega)/\omega$. The hyperfine weights and perpendicular spin components matter. The cited spin-chain paper supplies the response formula; it does not make that chain a superconducting-material example. NMR is not a momentum-resolved magnetic spectrum.

claims.statement: Mazin and colleagues proposed a compound-specific sign-changing extended-s state for fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. Their published note 8 revises the initial identification of the magnetic instability involved in the doping argument. Reading only the abstract can miss that qualification. Kuroki and colleagues' five-orbital RPA study likewise has parameter-dependent s- and d-wave competition. Neither result assigns one state to every iron-based material.

claims.statement: Kuroki's 2009 erratum corrects an orbital-to-band transformation error affecting the original gap plot. This check reads the erratum text, not a reproduction of its band calculation.
